findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dispenser parts of the soda machine were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- The PIC had an employee clean them and they were educated that the nozzles and the dispenser parts of the machine both need to be regularly cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: There were single service utensils and articles observed to be stored in the employee bathroom. CORRECTED- The PIC moved these items out of the bathroom and into an area suitable to store these items. Ensure that single service utensils and articles are properly stored to protect them from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(2) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT,UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (2) In toilet rooms.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility is observed to be using a Quaternary ammonium sanitizer and does not have test strips for it. Every sanitizer that is used in a facility should have test strips for it. A follow up is scheduled for 10/17/2025 to ensure that Quaternary ammonium test strips have been obtained.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The ice machine was observed to have a small accumulation of mold on the back side of the baffle.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure the baffle gets cleaned regularly to prevent contamination of the ice.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: 4-903.11:Observed box of single use cups stored directly on floor. (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160: Observed the ice scoop being stored on a box of garbage bags. Discussed with facility that the materials contacting the outside of boxes can never be determined and that they are assumed not clean. A clean bucket for the ice scoop is normally available for the scoop storage. Provided clean storage during inspection. Scoop pulled for cleaning.  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1310: Observed a can of window cleaner stored on top of an in-use box of single-service utensils. Cleaner was moved during the inspection.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 Ruby Gardria has passed her FSSMC exam and is awaiting the IDPH certificate.  All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 The facility does not have a certified food manager employed. The facility has had difficulty finding an interpreter and may need an extension past the February date. The second attempt at the FSSMC was taken November 4 and results have yet to be posted.  All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250 The facility has a honey butter being stored on a shelf over the preparation cooler. The bag and the bulk box both indicate to keep product refrigerated. Krispy Krunchy Chicken representative stated that the standard operational procedure is to store the product at room temperature and refrigerate at night. Facility refrigerated food during the inspection. Rep. indicated he would provide facility with documentation regarding safe food handling. In the meantime, keep squeeze bottles held in fridge.   All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540  Facility still has 90 days from pre-opening to correct the presence of a FSSMC. Owner has gone through the course and is going to make a second attempt at the test. Suggested that facility have at least two FSSMC present. All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed crates of drinks stored on the floor of the walk in cooler. Store all food, drinks, and service items at least 6" above the floor.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed a stack of coffee filters stored on top of a box next to the 3 part sink. Store coffee filters in a clean and covered container if removed from the original package.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
